title: Sound, Rudy Powell and Arthur Reeves
summary: Carter wanted Trumbauer's sound; Reeves taught emphasis on sound and articulation around 1923-24.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Uh huh. But these early lessons, then, would have been just concerned with just the fundamentals of the instrument; that is, the production of sound.
Now what kind of sound, I mean, you were listening to some of these records, but what kind of sound did he encourage you to try for on the Alto?

Well, the sound ... I don't remember exactly what he encouraged me to try for, but I was sort of after the sound of Frankie Trumbauer at that time, and if you're familiar with Rudy Powell, which you certainly must be, you know, Rudy is a very fine saxophone player, and although I studied some with him, and then with Lieutenant Mikel Michael, our sounds were, you know, quite different.

Yes. Of course, after Lieutenant Michael, I studied with a man named Arthur Reeves, who really hit -- his emphasis was on sound. You know, and on articulation. And he got a wonderful sound. I really wanted to sound like him.
Now this would have been roughly, when? I mean ...
Oh, let's see. I was born in 1907, and I guess we're getting around to about 1923,4, I guess, you know.
